correctness.rationale: Exchangeability plus absence of ties makes every labeled score ordering equiprobable. Collapsing labels to calibration/future type gives a uniform binary interleaving, which is bijective with weak compositions of the future count among calibration gaps. Stars-and-bars yields the Dirichlet-multinomial aggregation, and a prefix-count recurrence yields the band dynamic program. Exact exhaustive enumeration in verify.py checks the fine and aggregated laws, covariance, and dynamic program on finite cases.

originality.rationale: PASS: The closest inspected conformal source gives only a one-level beta-binomial empirical-coverage law; nested-set and tolerance-region sources provide the framework but not the finite joint multilevel law. Semantic searches using conformal, Dirichlet-multinomial, uniform-composition, order-statistic, and simultaneous-band formulations found no result that implies the full claim. The fine-gap law is proved directly, while novelty is asserted only for the conformal joint-law/band-evaluator formulation, not for classical Dirichlet-multinomial probability.
residual_risks: Classical multivariate tolerance-region or order-statistics literature may contain an equivalent spacing-count theorem under different terminology; the searches performed cannot rule out that possibility.

The ingredients of the proof are elementary and classical. The originality assessment is therefore restricted to the exact split-conformal multilevel identification and simultaneous-band evaluator, not the underlying distributions or stars-and-bars identities.

value.rationale: A single calibration sample is routinely used to report prediction sets at several nominal levels, whose empirical coverages are strongly dependent. The theorem supplies their exact finite-sample coupling, explicit cross-level covariance, and an exact \(O(nm)\) simultaneous-band evaluator for the whole coverage curve. This replaces marginal-only calculations or conservative union bounds with a natural complete rank-grid calculation; the scope is the full calibration hierarchy rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
